messages.content: Write a polished short scene in modern American English about two adult friends doing a simple task together at home. Let the scene balance dialogue, internal observation, and small physical actions. One character is distracted by something on their mind, but the scene should not become melodramatic or fully explain the problem. Keep the prose grounded, contemporary, and specific. Avoid generic filler and let the scene develop naturally through what the characters say and do.

Alex stood at the kitchen counter, trying to separate two grocery bags that had somehow tied themselves together.

“Need help?” Jordan asked.

“No.”

Jordan waited.

Alex pulled harder. The handles tightened.

“Still no?”

“I've got it.”

“You've been fighting that bag for thirty seconds.”

“It's losing.”

Jordan leaned against the counter. “Sure.”

Alex finally got the knot loose and set both bags down with more force than necessary.

Jordan glanced at her. “Everything okay?”

“Yep.”

“That was convincing.”

Alex opened one of the bags and started putting things away. “I'm just tired.”

Jordan nodded, letting that sit.

A box of cereal went into the cabinet. Then another. Alex stopped with a can of soup in her hand and stared at it for a second.

“What?” Jordan asked.

“Nothing.”

“You've been holding that soup for a while.”

Alex looked at the can. “I forgot where it goes.”

“You've lived here longer than I've known how to cook.”

“Fair point.”

She put the can in the pantry.

Jordan opened the refrigerator and started moving things around to make room for the milk.

“You're reorganizing again,” Alex said.

“There's no system in here.”

“There is absolutely a system.”

“Where?”

Alex pointed. “Dairy on the left.”

Jordan looked at the shelves. “That's not a system. That's a hostage situation.”

Alex laughed despite herself.

“There,” Jordan said. “That's better.”

“Don't get used to it.”

Jordan put the milk away and closed the door. For a moment neither of them said anything.

Alex looked toward the counter, then back at her.

“Thanks.”

Jordan shrugged. “I didn't do anything.”

“I know.”

Jordan nodded once. “Okay.”

Alex picked up the last bag.

“Where does the bread go?”

Jordan smiled. “You've got to be kidding.”

Alex smiled back. “I'm tired.”
